messages.content: Write a contemporary American fiction scene between two adult best friends eating takeout. Use interruptions, unfinished sentences, corrections, jokes, and thoughts that get abandoned when the conversation moves on. Do not make every exchange polished or perfectly complete.

“Did you order the—”

“Yeah.”

“The spicy one?”

“No, the regular.”

“Why would you order the regular?”

“Because you said—”

“I said extra spicy.”

“You said ‘a little spicy.’”

“I did not.”

“You absolutely did.”

Jordan opened the container and looked inside. “Fine. This is on me.”

Alex stole one of the dumplings from her plate.

“Hey.”

“You weren't eating it.”

“I was looking at it.”

“That's not ownership.”

“It was a visual relationship.”

Jordan stared at him. “You sound like a—”

“A what?”

“Never mind.”

“Now you have to tell me.”

“No.”

“Come on.”

She pointed her chopsticks at him. “Eat your food.”

He did, chewing as she opened the sauce packet.

“Oh, remember that thing on Saturday?” she said.

“What thing?”

“The thing with your cousin.”

Alex swallowed. “Oh. Right.”

“You were going to tell me—”

“I'll tell you later.”

“That usually means you forgot.”

“I didn't forget.”

“You forgot.”

He smiled. “Maybe.”

Jordan shook her head and reached for another dumpling. This time he didn't try to steal it.
